facts.fact: CAP theorem describes trade-offs between consistency, availability, and partition tolerance in distributed systems

CAP Theorem.mantra: Pick two: consistency, availability, or partition tolerance—you cannot have all three.
when: Designing distributed databases or data stores
Choosing replication strategies across regions
Evaluating consistency models for microservices
Handling network partition scenarios in cloud architectures
without: Assuming strong consistency with zero latency cost
Designing systems that silently lose data during partitions
Unexpected unavailability when prioritizing consistency
Stale reads surprising users in eventually consistent systems
CAP Theorem.tradeoff: Stronger consistency increases latency and reduces availability, while higher availability risks serving stale or conflicting data.

PACELC Theorem.mantra: Even when things are fine, you're still trading consistency for latency.
when: Choosing replication strategies for distributed databases
Designing multi-region data architectures
Evaluating eventual vs strong consistency models
Optimizing read latency across replicas
without: Unexpected latency spikes from strong consistency in distributed reads
Stale data served without understanding the trade-off
Over-engineered consistency where low latency matters more
Blind reliance on CAP theorem ignoring normal operation trade-offs
PACELC Theorem.tradeoff: Under normal operation, lower latency requires relaxing consistency, while strong consistency demands higher latency.
